Me, I am farming here in Tabora on my 6.37 hectares. The land is ours, and I mix crops together like we always do — it helps if one fails, the other gives something. The rains here come only once from November, and the soils are not like those of Mbeya; putting chemical fertilizer on this kind of plot with mixed crops is not how we do it, and the price is too high for a man like me. I will use the manure from the few animals we keep, plant the seeds I saved from last year, and call on some young men from the village to help me clear and weed because this is too much land for my family alone.
